s1.syndrome_frame: Congenital neurological condition with prenatal intracranial hemorrhage and postnatal neurological abnormalities
salient_findings: Intracranial hemorrhage detected on fetal ultrasound and MRI
Porencephalic cyst in the right frontotemporal-insular region
Mild upper limb hypertonicity and abnormal deep tendon reflexes
key_facts: Male neonate born at 38 weeks' gestation
Birth weight 2350g (5th-10th percentile)
Length 45cm (5th percentile)
Head circumference 31cm (<5th percentile)
Apgar scores 8 and 9 at 1 and 5 minutes
Maternal history of febrile episode in periconceptional period
Fetal ultrasound at 20 weeks suggested intracranial hemorrhage
Fetal MRI at 25 weeks confirmed porencephalic cyst
Normal laboratory studies including complete blood count and coagulation profile
Normal gene sequencing for MTHFR and factor V Leiden
Newborn metabolic screening negative
Cranial ultrasound on day 1 showed right porencephalic area and germinolytic cyst

Newborn metabolic screening negative

shortlist.label: Porencephaly
shortlist.why_kept: Fetal MRI at 25 weeks confirmed porencephalic cyst and cranial ultrasound on day 1 showed right porencephalic area

shortlist.label: Congenital cytomegalovirus infection
shortlist.why_kept: Maternal history of febrile episode in periconceptional period and maternal CMV serology at 11 weeks (IgG positive, IgM negative)

shortlist.label: Fetal stroke
shortlist.why_kept: Fetal ultrasound at 20 weeks suggested intracranial hemorrhage and fetal MRI at 25 weeks showed reduced right cerebral hemisphere volume

shortlist.label: Schizencephaly
shortlist.why_kept: Abnormal micropolygyria of the right frontal cortex on fetal MRI at 25 weeks

shortlist.label: Perinatal stroke
shortlist.why_kept: Intracranial hemorrhage suggested by fetal ultrasound at 20 weeks and confirmed by fetal MRI at 25 weeks

raw.rationale: Fetal ultrasound at 20 weeks and fetal MRI at 25 weeks confirmed a porencephalic cyst in the right frontotemporal-insular region, which is consistent with the diagnosis of porencephaly. The presence of a porencephalic area and a germinolytic cyst on cranial ultrasound and MRI at birth further supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Congenital cytomegalovirus infection
rejected.why: Maternal CMV serology was IgG positive and IgM negative, indicating past infection rather than recent infection, and there are no other indications of congenital CMV infection

rejected.label: Fetal stroke
rejected.why: While fetal ultrasound suggested intracranial hemorrhage, the presence of a porencephalic cyst is more consistent with porencephaly than with a stroke

rejected.label: Schizencephaly
rejected.why: There is no mention of a cleft or abnormality in the cerebral cortex, which is characteristic of schizencephaly

rejected.label: Perinatal stroke
rejected.why: The presence of a porencephalic cyst and germinolytic cyst on imaging studies, as well as the fetal ultrasound and MRI findings, suggest a prenatal rather than perinatal event
